title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
description: Max Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, detailed on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt how his company's work with PRIMA is part of its path toward a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).

title: Cerebras CEO says we’re nearing a future where everyone has a personal AI assistant at home
description: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman predicts a future where personal AI assistants become as commonplace as household appliances, running partly on local devices and partly in the cloud.

title: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks
description: Industrial Next helps manufacturers automate complex, delicate tasks that have traditionally required human labor.

title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
description: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman has a message for AI leaders spreading doomsday warnings: Maybe stop talking? At TechCrunch Disrupt, he argued that the industry's focus on AI's risks is drowning out its potential benefits.

title: Judge orders OpenAI to turn over hiring records in Apple trade secrets case
description: A federal judge ruled that Apple can access OpenAI's interview materials involving former Apple employees, as well as private messages and testimony from key figures in the case.

title: Flox Intelligence is building AI to keep wildlife away from trains, airports, and roads
description: Flox's edge devices can identify animals and use species-specific sounds to drive them away from critical infrastructure.

title: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm
description: Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” a feature it first launched on Instagram.

title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
description: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.

title: Pluto Security raises $42M as AI gives enterprise security teams a new headache
description: The problem with giving everyone in a company access to AI tools is that people will use them in unexpected ways. And that fact is steadily seeding fears that companies now have new, gaping security holes in their systems or, at least, will soon.

title: Google Play now lets anyone build private, vibe-coded apps that run on Android
description: Google is making it easier to build and use personal Android apps created with AI, without having to make them available to everyone on the Play Store.

title: SpaceX and Google both said no. Now his software is riding a SpaceX rocket next to Google’s
description: Satlyt wants to be the Android of orbital computing, offering open software that works on many companies' satellites, versus SpaceX's closed, all-in-one iPhone-style approach.

title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026: Day 1
description: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 officially kicks off today. See what's in store for Day 1 (Oct. 13) at San Francisco's Moscone West. Don't miss it. Register for your pass now and meet 10,000+ tech leaders at the startup epicenter of the year.

title: SpaceXSI bundles X Premium, Grok, and Cursor into one subscription
description: The new X Subscription combines X's paid features with AI tools like Grok and Cursor, offering plans ranging from $8 to $200 per month.

title: The final Disrupt Stage lineup: Three days of conversations you won’t hear anywhere outside of TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
description: The full TechCrunch Disrupt Stage lineup revealed, featuring Max Hodak, Mark Wahlberg, Benchmark partners, and more. Register now to save up to $100 on your pass and get a second at 50% off.

title: Amex introduces a framework to prevent AI agents from making unauthorized purchases
description: American Express is introducing a new framework designed to ensure AI agents only make purchases their users have authorized, potentially preventing costly mistakes and disputes as AI-powered shopping grows.

title: Just 5 years in, interactive chatbot platform Character.AI files for bankruptcy
description: The startup will sell some of its assets to Disney for $20 million.

title: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder
description: Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding.

title: WindBorne wins a hefty US Air Force contract for its balloon data
description: A Silicon Valley startup that uses weather balloons and AI to predict the weather won a U.S. military contract worth almost $50 million.

title: Honeyjar offers AI tools to improve PR and comms at every company
description: Journalists, entrepreneurs, and even some public relations professionals will tell you that the PR process is broken. But could AI actually make things better?

title: Microsoft president says UK is best placed to drive AI regulation
description: Microsoft president Brad Smith calls for urgent AI regulation, saying milk and washing machines have more oversight than AI companies.
